page: Microsoft Azure E48_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Ev3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor, operating at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 50 MB of L3 cache, 32 KB of L1d cache, and 0.25 MB of L2 cache. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 1229 GB SSD, while no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is constrained, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% and bottom 25% categories respectively. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by the stress-ng multi-core score of 23299.53 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8655.0. Memory bandwidth is stable, with read-only large block speeds reaching 117.37 GB/sec and write speeds at 49.49 GB/sec, both placing in the middle 50% of tested systems.

The hardware profile presents a clear tradeoff: while single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and text processing are weak, the high memory capacity and 48 vCPUs support parallelized workloads. Database operations and Redis SET operations perform at average levels, with Redis achieving 27.95 million operations per second. Large language model inference is limited, showing weak text generation speeds across 135M and 7B models. This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive applications that require large datasets in RAM but do not demand high single-thread CPU performance. It is recommended for relational databases, in-memory caching, and multi-threaded data processing.
